requirement:
The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
in `used`, as described in {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.mcp.description`.
rationale:
The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]` covers each obligation of `requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions`.

- **First result includes `instructions`, even when `matches` is empty.**
  - In `session`, the first successful `search_text` call is for `absent`, which has no matches. The test reads `empty["instructions"]` and asserts that it contains the expected phrases.
  - In a separate `fresh` session, the first `search_text` call is for `hit`, which has matches. The test asserts `hits["instructions"] == instructions`.
- **Text and structural searches share the rule.** In `peer`, the first call is `search_structure` with an empty result. The test asserts that `page["instructions"]` equals the same instructions string.
- **Failed searches leave the instructions for the first successful delivery.**
  - In `session`, `search_text` with the invalid pattern `(` is asserted to return an error.
  - The next successful search, `absent`, still carries `instructions`.
  - This failure case is only exercised through `search_text`. A failed structural search is not tested, but the requirement states one shared rule, so I do not treat that as a gap.
- **Later searches omit the field.**
  - In `peer`, a later `search_text` call has no `instructions`.
  - In `session`, the later `hit` search, which is not the first search in that session, asserts `first.get("instructions").is_none()`.
- **Continuation pages omit the field.** Both `get_next_page` results, `rest` and `second`, assert that `instructions` is absent.
- **Instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include in `used`.** The test asserts the phrases "Before submitting, close every delivered search page", "finish_search", "tags for excerpts you relied on without a separate source read", "used:[] if none qualify, including an empty result" and "without reading more source". Together these cover when to finish and which tags to list. The cited `finish_search.mcp.description` text is context only and is not reassessed here.
- **Per-conversation scoping.** Two independent `SessionTools` instances, `fresh` and `peer`, each receive their own first-delivery instructions after another session has already had its first search.

The assertions check actual output values rather than just running the code, so I found no gap.

text: The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
> `Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets you used to
> justify your conclusion without an additional source read. search_id is the
> result's UUID and used is an array of its short entry tags, e.g.
> whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use
> used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search. Every delivered
> search must be finished before submission. The result is {search_id,
> finished:true}; no additional source is delivered.`
